name: Global Title
epitaph: PRIME's Global Title was first won by Alex Caine on 6 July 2003. The fed's own record carries 10 reigns on it, across 8 different champions. The longest is Ignatius Lisieux's, 152 days from 23 February 2004. Two of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. PRIME renamed it the Universal Title on 26 September 2004.

events.note: PRIME's own title history: 'At this point in time, the Global title ceased to be, and the top prize in PRIME was declared the Universal Championship.' The Universal section opens 'Black Angel declared inaugural champion after vacation of Global Title at King of Kings 2 (9/26/04)' and continues the Global's own numbering. Source: PRIME's own Title Histories page.
events.title: prime-2003-universal

notes: PRIME's own Title Histories page, its 'GLOBAL TITLE (DEFUNCT)' section: ten numbered reigns, 6 July 2003 – 26 September 2004; the Universal section continues its numbering from '1. (11.)'.

name: Universal Title
epitaph: PRIME's Universal Title was first won by Black Angel on 26 September 2004. The fed's own record carries 22 reigns on it, across 17 different champions. The longest is Jason Snow's, 401 days from 13 March 2009. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. Hessian held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Intense Title
epitaph: PRIME's Intense Title was first won by Rock Startling on 6 July 2003. The fed's own record carries 31 reigns on it, across 28 different champions. The longest is Vangelus Olsig's, 361 days from 24 July 2005. Five of its reigns ended outside a match — stripped from the holder or vacated. Its last champion, Seymour Almasy, vacated it on 1 August 2011.

name: 5 Star Title
epitaph: PRIME's 5 Star Title was first won by Mark Blaze on 23 June 2003. The fed's own record carries 31 reigns on it, across 25 different champions. The longest is Tyler Rayne's, 275 days from 30 January 2008. Three of its reigns ended outside a match — stripped from the holder. Roxy Phoenix held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Alias Title
epitaph: PRIME's Alias Title was first won by JTF on 3 March 2004, who became its Xposure Champion; its first four champions carried it under names of their own — Xposure, roC-TV, PRIMEal Rage and PRIMEtime — and the fed's own cards and title log also bill it the Pulse Title and the Internet Title. The fed's own record carries 14 reigns on it, across 14 different champions. The longest is The Illustrious Face-Eater's, 189 days from 16 November 2005. Three of its reigns ended outside a match — retired with the belt or vacated. PRIME merged it into the 5 Star Title on 30 May 2007.

events.note: The fed's own page, closing the 'ALIAS TITLE (DEFUNCT)' section: 'At ReVolution 129, in the "Champions Collide" match, The Supreme Machine (5-Star Champion) defeated Easton Hall (Alias Champion) and Dusk (Intense Champion) in a triple threat match. Sirrajin was declared the final Alias Champion and then the title was merged with the 5-Star Title.' The fed's own title log carries the change but no row for the merge itself. Source: The fed's own card, ReVolution of 30 May 2007, 'Champions Collide: Killean Sirrajin (5-Star) vs. Dusk (Intense) vs. Easton Hall (Alias)', and PRIME's own Title Histories page.
events.title: prime-2003-5-star

name: Tag Team Title
epitaph: PRIME's Tag Team Title was first won by Mark Blaze & Andy Magnum on 14 September 2003. The fed's own record carries 34 reigns on it, across 31 different champions. The longest is Crudely Civilized's, 134 days from 12 March 2004. Four of its reigns ended outside a match — handed over or vacated. Change in Spades held it at the end of the surviving record. PRIME suspended its tag division after Culture Shock 2010.

name: Internet Title
epitaph: PRIME's own title log files four reigns under the Internet Title between May and September 2006 — The Illustrious Face-Eater's, then Tony Gamble's from 24 May, Jonathon Winters' from 8 July and Adam's from 19 September — and its own title history lists the same changes, on the same nights, as reigns of the Alias Title.
notes: The fed's own title log, five rows under the Internet Title, 24 May – 19 September 2006; its own title history, Alias Title entries 8–11.

name: Dual Halo
epitaph: PRIME's annual two-ring elimination match at Culture Shock, whose winner took a guaranteed wish, the Golden Ticket. The fed's own Records & Superlatives page lists seven winners, one a year from 2004 to 2010.

name: Jewel in the Crown
epitaph: A tournament PRIME ran once a year from 2003 to 2009, its seven winners listed on the fed's own Records & Superlatives page. By its Hall of Fame page, the first, Ian English, took an automatic Global Title shot from it, at ReVolution 18.
